items.q: Which platforms does it work with?
items.a: PC, PS3, PS4, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2 and the original arcade cabinet. In MIDI mode it also plays as a USB MIDI drum in any music software. Pick the mode from the OLED menu or the web configurator.

items.q: Do I need to install software?
items.a: No. Put the drum in keyboard mode (Keyboard P1 or P2), plug it in and open the configurator in a WebSerial browser (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Firefox). Everything is also adjustable from the OLED on the E-box.

items.q: My drum registers hits I didn't make. What do I do?
items.a: Lower the sensitivity for that pad, from the OLED menu or the configurator's live monitor, where you can watch each pad's readings in real time.

items.q: Can I use the Onigiri-con with another drum?
items.a: Yes. It's also compatible with TaikoForce and ZhongTaiko drums.
Yes: firmware, hardware and this configurator are on GitHub. You can even build your own.

closing.tagline: 12 mm birch plywood, Italian galvanized steel, open-source brain

items.title: Real arcade rubber
items.body: The head is real arcade rubber, the same kind used on arcade cabinets, so it feels like the drum you already know.

items.title: Galvanized steel plates
items.body: Four plates, a center and a rim on each side, cut in Italy from 3 mm galvanized sheet steel. Firm under the stick, with plenty of bounce.

items.title: Birch plywood
items.body: A 12 mm birch body, sourced and cut in Italy and assembled by hand. Stiff, resonant and built to take a beating.

items.title: Lighter, steadier stand
items.body: Less weight, a wider footprint, no wobble on hard hits. The cradles on the front hold your bachi, so your sticks are always within reach.
